narrative: You asked about appeal overturn dollar rate, and this answer publishes no finding for it. It was measured — it is on the charts and in the evidence below — and no cell of it survived selection, so nothing above speaks for it. What follows measures the other things this question read. Atlas Commercial denials account for $98,700.66 in overturned denied dollars over Feb 1–Jul 31, 2026, measured directly (F1). All of that sits with Atlas Commercial itself — 100.0% of the total, calculated from measured values (F2) — so there is no other payer inside this result to compare it against. Read that figure as dollars put back in play rather than recovered cash, and as appeal state at the latest data load (F1); denials near the edge of the window show little overturn activity simply because their appeals have not been decided yet, which means the $98,700.66 reflects what has been decided so far rather than the full outcome of the pipeline (F2). Every figure this answer publishes for the current window is measured. The comparison window is not: 4 of its cells are too small to measure exactly — fewer than 11 of the events being counted landed in each, over a population this answer publishes in full — so each shows a ceiling instead of a figure: COB (appeal overturn rate ≤ 90.9% over 11 entities); DUPLICATE (appeal overturn rate ≤ 71.4% over 14 entities); ELIGIBILITY (appeal overturn rate ≤ 52.6% over 19 entities); MEDICAL_NECESSITY (appeal overturn rate ≤ 62.5% over 16 entities). The true value is at or below the ceiling and is not a measurement. A further 4 could not be published at all.

probes.purpose: Overturn rate per payer, counted and dollar-weighted. Both divide by DECIDED appeals only, so pending appeals never dilute them.
Where appeals win by root-cause category — the input to "appeal more of this, prevent more of that".

Pipeline size and two different failures side by side: pending share is filed work awaiting a payer decision (denominator is filed appeals), unworked share is denials never touched at all (denominator is workable denials), given both counted and dollar-weighted because the money left on the table is rarely proportional to the records left alone. Recent populations read high on both shares by construction.
Dollars whose denial was reversed against total denied dollars. Overturned dollars are an upper bound on recovery, not posted cash — no stored linkage ties an appeal outcome to a later payment.
